competitive_landscape: The Andaman is served by a dense fleet of speedboats and ferries to Phi Phi, Krabi and Phang Nga — crowded, often rough, and grounded for much of the SW monsoon. The cross-border link to Langkawi is a slow, seasonal ferry. Comfort, weather-resilience and the long cross-border leg are the open gaps.

regulatory_note: Operations fall under the Thai Marine Department and Marine National Park rules (including seasonal closures), with cross-border legs touching Thai and Malaysian CIQ at established jetties.
seasonality: The SW monsoon (roughly May–Oct) brings rough Andaman seas and many island closures; high season is Nov–Apr. Foiling extends the comfortable operating window, and Quanta-LR range gives routing flexibility across monsoon conditions.

summary: Phuket anchors the Andaman: Phi Phi, Phang Nga Bay, Krabi and the Similan group are all high-demand hops handled by Pioneer II, while Quanta-LR's hybrid range opens the cross-border Andaman corridor to Langkawi. It is the natural SEA west-coast counterpart to the Bali cluster.
tagline: The Andaman hub — islands close in, a cross-border corridor reaching out.
transit_planning: For an authority or operator: a premium, low-emission water tier relieving the crowded Andaman speedboat corridors, plus a cross-border luxury line to Langkawi.
